standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma labelled lemma-base-change-one-step, source line 879 (Stacks tag 05H7)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the one-step half of the conclusion, quoted at proof lines 1288-1290; the remaining cokernel and condition-(2) arguments stay inside the counted span.

core_obligations: Reduce the assertion to two base change statements: quote the one step base change lemma to see that each primed tuple is again a one step devissage, and observe that only the formation of Coker(alpha_k) and condition (2) of the complete-devissage definition still have to be checked (proof lines 1288-1295).

Check the cokernel: pi'_{k,*}G'_k is the pullback of pi_{k,*}G_k by affine base change, and tensor product is right exact, so formation of Coker(alpha_k) commutes with the base change (proof lines 1295-1299).

Check condition (2): identify (pi'_{k,*}G'_k)_{xi'_k} tensor kappa(xi'_k) with the base change of (pi_{k,*}G_k)_{xi_k} tensor kappa(xi_k) along kappa(xi_k) -> kappa(xi'_k), which preserves the rank condition (proof lines 1299-1309).
proof_roadmap: Quote the one step base change lemma for (Z_k, Y_k, i_k, pi_k, G_k) so that the primed tuples are one step devissages after base change (proof lines 1288-1291).
Two conditions remain: that Coker(alpha_k) base changes, which follows from pi'_{k,*}G'_k being the pullback of pi_{k,*}G_k together with right exactness of tensor product (proof lines 1291-1299).

Condition (2) of the complete-devissage definition is preserved because the fibre of the primed pushforward at xi'_k is the scalar extension of the unprimed one along the residue-field extension (proof lines 1299-1309).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that after an arbitrary affine base change S' -> S every member of a complete devissage family (Z_k, Y_k, i_k, pi_k, G_k, alpha_k)_{k=1..n} has a primed counterpart that is again a complete devissage of the pulled-back pair F'/X'/S' (statement lines 1272-1284). The reduction to the one step case is immediate, but the two remaining conditions have to be checked through the pushforward: the cokernel of alpha_k must commute with base change, which is not formal because Coker is formed after the finite morphism pi_k, and condition (2) must be preserved through the residue-field extension kappa(xi_k) -> kappa(xi'_k) at the generic points of the fibres (proof lines 1295-1309). Both steps are short and consist of identifying a fibre of a pullback with a scalar extension, which is why the claim is H2.
